findings.F1: The short side earns nothing and the long side carries the whole book. In the trending regime, short bars average a gain of 0.000174 per bar (t 0.53, n 2535, mean allocation −0.27), while long bars average 0.001244 (t 4.71, n 5918, mean allocation 0.41). Across all bars, shorts summed 0.43 against 7.38 for longs.
findings.F2: Shorts deepen the falls that sink Calmar. The deepest fall is in w5 (−24.5%, the worst 20-day book sum −0.124). There shorts lost −0.58 against −0.29 for longs, and XRP alone lost −0.67 while its price rose 0.33. In 2023, shorts lost −0.639 while the coins' mean daily return was +0.0015 and the book's was −0.000192.
findings.F3: The coins do drift down after a negative 30-day run above the 200-day average, but only against their own average. Trending grid cases with a 30-day return ≤ 0 have a 10-day excess return of −0.024 (t −2.39, n 175). Shorting them still yields almost nothing (F1), because the coins' mean rise offsets the shortfall.
findings.F4: The fade at extreme runs is real in the raw 30-day return but missed by the standardised forecast. On trending grid cases with a positive 30-day return, the 10-day excess return is +0.044 (t 1.84) in the 26–45% quintile and −0.006 (t −0.24) above 45%. Long bars with a 30-day return above 40% gain 0.000189 per bar against 0.001998 for 7–40%, yet they still hold an allocation of 0.38 against 0.50. Meanwhile the standardised s ≥ 14 bucket shows no fade (s≥14 minus 8≤s<14: −0.0095, t −0.38).
findings.F5: The book's worst days come from large longs held after big runs. On the worst 5% of book days, the book is long on 68% of coin-bars (32% on other days), with mean allocation 0.26 (0.09), mean 30-day return 0.23 (0.04) and mean s 9.4 (6.3).
findings.F6: Among trending cases with a positive 30-day return, the gain shows up mostly where the 10-day run is also strongest. The top 10-day-return quartile has a 10-day excess return of +0.049 (t 2.18, n 114), while the other quartiles lie between −0.001 and +0.014 (|t| ≤ 1.13).

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average and its 30-day return is positive, the larger that 30-day return, the larger its rise over the next 10 days, except at its very largest 30-day returns, where the larger that return, the smaller the rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold only longs above the long average, sized up with the month-long run, and would stop shorting the uptrend's pullbacks, since those shorts add falls and no gain.
ideas.name: long-only monthly run drift

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average, the larger its 30-day percent gain, the larger its rise over the next 10 days, except where that gain is largest as a share of the price itself, where the larger the 30-day percent gain, the smaller the rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would cut the long as the raw month-long gain becomes very large, rather than judging the run only against its own recent range, which keeps him fully long into the falls.
ideas.name: raw run fade above average

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average and its 30-day return is positive, the larger its 10-day return, the larger its rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would add to a long in an uptrend when the latest ten days carry the run, and stay light when the month's gain is old.
ideas.name: fresh run carries drift
